Derived-key checks use TYPES_MAP independently and therefore must not be assumed to accept booleans after this proposal.

spec.question: We are considering allowing Python booleans wherever the signature validator accepts the JMESPath `number` type. The proposed implementation adds `'bool'` to the `number` entry in `REVERSE_TYPES_MAP`, so signatures using `array-number` inherit the same allowance. No function body, type-reporting mapping, arity rule, or expression-reference key validation would change. Which existing tests would newly fail with exactly this change?
